correctness.rationale: The source declares a Caputo-Fabrizio model and its existence section explicitly uses the associated Losada--Nieto integral with a local term plus an ordinary time integral. For the exact scalar rodent-total equation, that integral implies initial compatibility at equilibrium for a continuous solution and otherwise a right jump followed by an ordinary exponential transient. The source's displayed Mittag-Leffler boundedness transient is instead the classical Caputo solution. Likewise, the printed Adams--Bashforth--Moulton method uses the power-law Volterra weights of the Diethelm--Ford--Freed Caputo scheme. An independent algebra replay with positive generic coefficients verifies the CF right-limit and exponential rate, so the operator mismatch is mathematical rather than terminological.

evidence: Diethelm--Ford--Freed cover the classical Caputo predictor-corrector.
Losada--Nieto define the CF-associated integral, and later CF theory discusses its initial-time structure.

Diethelm--Ford--Freed explicitly derive their predictor-corrector for the classical Caputo derivative and its power-law Volterra equation. Targeted correction and Resultary searches found no published source-specific operator correction.
